conclusion.root_cause: The prompt itself is not broken. Workspace.Map.Station.Lobby.MissionBoard.BoardPrompt is enabled, has hold 0 and a range of 16, and a probe client triggered it while standing in range. A server-side Triggered listener received that trigger (dbgFired went from 0 to 1), and the MissionBoard tag is present. So the judge's report that the prompt never fires is a testing artefact. The cause of the missing round is the lobby design: the board prompt only opens or selects a mission in the board UI, and in the probes it did not start a mission (InstanceId stayed "" and RoundState stayed "Lobby"). A round only launches when a squad forms on a SquadPad, the countdown reaches 0, and LobbyService:Launch calls MissionService:StartMission. A tester that triggers only the board never gets a launch, so no fires, rescues or rounds_completed counters appear. I did not read the BoardPrompt.Triggered handler body, because the file output was truncated. The fix belongs in LobbyService.
conclusion.evidence: Client probe: p:InputHoldBegin()/InputHoldEnd() fired Triggered once with enabled=true and dist 6.6. Server probe: a Triggered listener on the same prompt counted the trigger (before=0, after=1) and the board part carries the MissionBoard tag. After triggering, InstanceId and SquadId stayed "", workspace RoundState stayed "Lobby", and no round started. The prompt-to-server path works, and launching depends on the squad and pad flow in LobbyService.
conclusion.fix_hint: In LobbyService's MissionBoard BoardPrompt.Triggered handler, make triggering the board start a round for a player who is not on a pad. Auto-join the player to a squad via Join, Choose firstEnabled(), and call Launch (or LobbyService:Launch with the first enabled mission). Alternatively, give the player clear feedback to step on a SquadPad, and have the test harness use the _join and _launch hooks.

conclusion.root_cause: Unproven, and I could not run a probe. The best-supported hypothesis is that the Mission Board 'Pick a call' ProximityPrompt is not usable as built. It is probably disabled, parented to a part that is not reachable or not in range, or created before LobbyService looks it up. LobbyService therefore never receives Triggered, no round starts, and no fire, rescue or round counters are ever emitted. This may also be a testing artefact: the playtest harness may not be triggering the prompt the way a real player would. The earlier LobbyService patch applied no edits, so I am pointing at the builder that creates the Mission Board and its prompt instead.
conclusion.evidence: No probe results. The only evidence is the anomaly report: the prompt never fires, and the counters hold only setup values with no round counters. A previous fix to LobbyService produced 'no edits', which suggests the cause is not a simple change in that file.
conclusion.fix_hint: In StationBuilder, make sure the Mission Board prompt is Enabled, has a reasonable MaxActivationDistance, RequiresLineOfSight=false and HoldDuration of 0 to 1 second, and is parented to a Part in Workspace. Make sure it carries the tag or name that LobbyService connects to.

conclusion.root_cause: Most likely a testing artefact, not a game bug. On the playtest client, a fresh plain ProximityPrompt (HoldDuration 0, 4 studs from the player, no line-of-sight requirement) also never fires PromptShown, Triggered or PromptTriggered. The Gear Rack prompts are configured correctly: Enabled, MaxActivationDistance 9, HoldDuration 0, RequiresLineOfSight false, Style Custom with the InvPrompt attribute, and the player was 3.4 studs away. A prompt that is never shown on this client cannot be triggered by InputHoldBegin, so the 'does not trigger' result comes from the harness. The server-side grab logic in InventoryService (Triggered handler gated by InvPrompt) was not shown to be broken. I could not read the client InventoryController, which draws the Custom prompts, so a client-side drawing issue is not ruled out. I did not test a server-side Triggered or Give call, so I did not prove that the grab itself works.
conclusion.evidence: Probe 3: the rack prompt did not trigger and InvHand stayed empty. Probe 4: the control prompt (control=false) and the rack prompt (rack=false) both failed in the same spot. conclusion.fix_hint: No game code change is clearly needed. To verify, trigger the grab server-side with InventoryService._give(player, 'axe') or fire the prompt's Triggered handler, or retest with a real player input. If real players really cannot grab, check that InventoryController renders the Custom-style prompts and that the server Triggered handler in InventoryService runs.

-- (docs/game/08 "Inventory"). Gear is real stuff in the world: station GearRacks, truck compartments,
-- the truck's hose reel, and anything dropped or thrown. Slot rules live in ReplicatedStorage/Lib/Items/
-- ItemDefs (spec-tested); the item looks in Lib/Items/ItemProps.
--
-- Slots: HAND (one held item = a Tool under the character, made by ToolService:CreateTool so spraying
--   and the axe keep working), BACK (one backable item, the oxygen tank by default; a welded model on

--   RescueService's).
--
-- Public API:
--   InventoryService:Give(player, itemId): boolean      -- a fresh item, by the ItemDefs grab rules
--   InventoryService:Drop(player): boolean              -- G: carried prop first, else the hand item
--   InventoryService:Throw(player, aim: Vector3, charge: number): boolean
--   InventoryService:Swap(player): boolean              -- hand <-> back
--   InventoryService:GetHand(player): string?   GetBack(player): string?
--   InventoryService:Clear(player)                      -- silently empties every slot (no drops)
-- Signals: Changed(player), Bonked(thrower: Player, victim: Player, what: string),

		end
	end
	local f = hoseLineCache and hoseLineCache[fn]

	end
	local ok, res = pcall(f, ...)
